originalGroup.material:
Archived Photo Captions 013

The history club found a photograph labelled "The school garden, 1988." It showed pupils beside young trees. The club wanted to use it in an anniversary display. A retired teacher recognised a building in the background and said it had not opened until 1991. This made the written date doubtful.
Pupils checked a box of school newsletters. They found a similar tree-planting photograph in a 1993 issue, but the clothes and positions were different. It could show another event rather than prove the date of the first photograph. They also asked the archive volunteer to check the original envelope. It had no date.
The club displayed the photograph with a careful caption: "Garden planting event, date not confirmed." A note described the conflict between the old label and the building’s opening date. The pupils invited visitors with further evidence to contact the archive. They did not replace one uncertain date with another just because it seemed likely.

Pupils checked a box of school newsletters. They found a similar tree-planting photograph in a 1993 issue, but the clothes and positions were different. It could show another event rather than prove the date of the first photograph. They also asked the archive volunteer to check the original envelope. It had no date.
The club displayed the photograph with a careful caption: "Garden planting event, date not confirmed." A note described the conflict between the old label and the building’s opening date. The pupils invited visitors with further evidence to contact the archive. They did not replace one uncertain date with another just because it seemed likely.

originalGroup.material:
Reading Pages Challenge 013

The library’s reading challenge first counted pages. Pupils wrote the title and number of pages they had read each week. One pupil finished a large-print book with wide margins and gained more page points than a classmate reading the same story in a small edition. The story was equally long, but the page layouts were different.
The librarian did not accuse either pupil of cheating. Both had followed the rule. Instead, she changed the next round. Pupils would record reading time and write a short note about something they understood. The old page totals remained as records of that round, with an explanation of their limits. The new method still could not measure every part of reading, but it gave pupils more than one way to show their effort.
